 Judgment
The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the
injuries sustained by her in a road accident dated 11.01.2020.
2. The case of the Petitioner in brief

is that, on 11.01.2020 at about 08.00 a.m., the petitioner was pedestrian and crossing the NH150(A) road at Viswanathapura Male, Turuvekere Taluk,
Tumakuru District, slowly, carefully and cautiously observing all moving vehicles, at that time the rider of the Royal Bullet motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA42X8120 came at high speed in a rash and negligent manner without following any traffic rules and regulations so as to endanger human life and property, all of a sudden came from Mayasandra side and dashed against her, due to impact,
she was fell down and sustained severe injuries and immediately she was shifted to Turuvekere Govt. Hospital wherein first aid treatment was given and then shifted to Adichunchangiri Hospital,
B.G.Nagar, where admitted as an inpatient on 11.01.2020.

The duty doctors took xrays and examined her clinically and radiologically and diagnosed that she has sustained (L) supracondylar Humerus fracture with Intra articular exten, with comminuted fracture of lower end of (L) Ulna with Distal Radio Ulna joint decriptor with (L) side 6th, 7th ribs fracture with Linear Minimally displaced fracture and other injuries and underwent ORIF with C.C. screw for (L) Humerus, ORIF with Kwife for (L) Ulna and other injuries treated conservatively and discharged on 05.02.2020 with an advise.

So far she has spent Rs.2,75,000/ towards Hospital charges, medicines,
conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental expenses.
She has to undergo few more corrective and implant removal operations in future and she has to spend huge amount for future treatment.
3. The petitioner further stated that, at the time of accident she was doing agriculture and milk vending and earning more than Rs.15,000/ per month.
Due to the accidental injuries she is not able to do any work till this day and undergoing huge pecuniary loss and undergoing great mental shock, agony, discomfort and financial loss.
Due to fractures of left hand and ribs she is facing problems and has lost her normal activeness.
The Turuvekere Police have registered a criminal case and filed charge sheet against the driver of the said Royal Bullet motorcycle in Cr.No.7/2020 u/Sec.279 and 337 of IPC.
The 1st respondent being the RC owner and the 2 nd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to her.

2 4.
In response to the summons, the Respondents have appeared through their respective counsels and filed written statement.

5. The Respondent No.1 in the written statement has denied the averments made in para No.8,10,11,12,13,14,21 and 22(a) to (d) are as false and submitted that he holds the valid driving licence and he had insured his vehicle with the Respondent No.2 and the insurance policy was in effect on the alleged date of accident.
Therefore prayed for dismissal of the petition against him.

6. The Respondent No.2 in the written statement have denied have denied the case of the petitioner as false and admitted issuance of policy but their liability is subject to terms and conditions and submitted that there is a delay in lodging complaint and the FIR is lodged belatedly in order to search and falsely implicate the vehicle in the accident.

Further submitted that the rider of the insured vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of the accident, as such there is a violation of terms and conditions of the policy and there is non compliance of Sections 134(C), 158(6) of M.V. Act.
Therefore prayed for dismissal of the petition against them.

7. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that she met with a motor vehicle accident on 11.01.2020 at about 8.00 a.m., near Vishwanathapura Male village, on NH150(A)
road, Turuvekere Taluk, Tumakuru District and sustained grievous injuries due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Royal Bullet motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA 42X8120 ?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.

What order or award?
8.
The Petitioner in order to prove her case, she has examined herself as PW.1 and got marked documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.10.
Govindaraju J. Medical Record officer at Adichunchanagiri Hospital, Mandaya District, is examined as PW.2 and produced documents as per Exs.P11 to P.13.
Dr.Nagaraj B.N Orthopedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Center, is examined as PW.3 and produced documents as per Exs.P.14 and P.15.
On the other side, the respondent No.1 has examined himself as RW.1, but not produced any documents on his behalf.
The respondent No.2 has not lead any evidence on their behalf.

9. Heard the arguments and perused the materials on record.
10.

On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows: Issue No.1: In the affirmative, Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative, Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following: REASONS Smt.Rathnamma @ vs Sri.Harshit S on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166515967/
3 11. Issue No.1: The Petitioner in order to prove that the accident was occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Royal Bullet motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA42 X8120 has examined herself as PW.1 and produced 5 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.3, P5 and P6.

She has specifically stated in her evidence that, she was crossing NH150(A) road at Viswanathapura Male,
Turuvekere Taluk, Tumakuru District, cautiously observing all moving vehicles, at that time the rider of the Royal Bullet motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA42X8120 came at high speed in rash and negligent manner and all of a sudden came from Mayasandra side and dashed against her and caused the accident.

On the other side, the Respondents have denied the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and specifically contended that there was negligence on the part of the petitioner herself.
In the crossexamination of the PW.1 nothing worth is elicited to disbelieve the alleged manner of accident.

12. In support of the defence the respondent No.1 has examined himself as RW.1 who has deposed the contents of his written statement in his examination in chief and further deposed that there was no zebra crossing at the alleged place of accident and the petitioner herself was not cautious while crossing the road and the alleged accident took place due to sole negligence of the petitioner.
In the cross examination of RW.1 it is brought out that he has not lodged any first information before the police.
13. The respondent No.2 has not lead any evidence in support of their defence.

Further, the Petitioner apart from her oral evidence has produced the documents such as FIR and Complaint in Cr.No.0007/2020 of Turuvekere Police Station, complaint, spot mahazar, IMV report and chargesheet as per Exs.P.1 to P.3, P5 and P.6.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.3, P5 and P.6 and appreciating them which are public documents having presumptive value under law, in absence of contrary evidence this court is of the opinion that the driver of the offending vehicle driven it with rash or negligent manner and caused accident as alleged by the claimant.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:

The Petitioner has further averred that, on account of accident, she cannot lift or hold weight from her left hand, cannot raise her left hand above the shoulder level, restriction of pronation or supination, cannot do any manual work involving her left hand, cannot bend her body forwards or backward, cannot sit for longer duration cannot sleep on left side, painful and difficult to breath and she is suffering from permanent disability and hence she is unable to do her earlier work/occupation.
The Petitioner in this regard has entered into witness box and deposed that due to the accidental injuries, she is suffering from permanent disability.
Apart from that, she has produced the wound certificate as per Ex.P.4.

As per Ex.P.4, the petitioner has sustained tenderness over left fracture of left elbow, tenderness over both knee, abrasion over right cheek and forehead and abrasion over right and left knee, the doctor opined that injuries are grievous in nature.

The petitioner has got examined Govindaraju U.Medical Record Officer as PW.3 and Dr.Nagaraj B.N.
as PW.4.
This court while considering the Issue No.1 has already come to the conclusion that the accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of the driver of Royal Bullet motorcycle.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation from the Respondents.
Smt. Rathnamma

@ vs Sri.Harshit S on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166515967/
4 DISABILITY:-
15. The PW.2 - Govindaraju
Medical
Record
Officer at Adichunchanagiri Hospital, Mandaya, is examined as PW.2, who has MLC extract, police intimation and case sheet as per Exs.P.11 to 13.
In the cross examination of PW.2 it is only brought out that he has not produced any authorization letter issued by hospital and Ex.P.12 does not bear seal.
16. The PW.3 - Dr.Nagaraj B.N. Orthopedic surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Center, is examined as PW.3, who has produced xray film and clinical notes as per Exs.P.14 and P15.

He has deposed that,
the petitioner gave an alleged H/O RTA on 11.01.2020 and sustained left supracondylar humerus fracture with intraarticular extension with comminuted fracture of the lower end of the left ulna and distal radioulnar joint disruptions with left sided 6th and 7th rib fracture with linear minimally displaced fracture involving anterior column of the right acetabulum and as per the discharge summary the petitioner was treated at Adichunchanagiri Hospital with ORIF with CC screws for the left Humerus and Kwire for the left Ulna and later discharged she said she was on regular follow up in the same hospital and the Kwire was removed from the left ulna and left elbow developed deformity and instability.

The PW.3 has further deposed that the petitioner now complaints of deformed left elbow, unable to do any work in the left upper limb, needs support for every day to day activity and on examined the petitioner has cubitus varus deformity at the left elbow, restricted and unstable left elbow movements and recent xray of the left elbow shows malunited fracture of the left lower humerus condyle with implant in situ and he examined clinically, radiologically and assessment of disability, he is of the opinion that the petitioner has got permanent disability of the left arm at 67% and to the whole body is 22%, which is permanent in nature and the petitioner needs another surgery for removal of the implant and re construct the left elbow which cost around Rs.1,20,000/.

In the crossexamination of PW.3 it is brought out that he has not treated the petitioner, he has assessed only physical disability of the petitioner and he has not seen the follow up treatment records of the petitioner.

Therefore, considering the nature of injury, treatment taken,
evidence lead, age of the petitioner the 22% of whole body disability deposed by the PW.3 appears to be on higher side.
The PW.3 only deposed about the physical disability and not deposed as to how it affects the work of the petitioner.
The discharge summary shows that at the time of discharge the condition of the petitioner was satisfactory.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, the period of treatment that she has undergone, her age, the functional disability is considered at 14% to the whole body.
Monthly income 17.
The Petitioner has deposed in her evidence that, she was doing agriculture work and milk vending and earning more than Rs.15,000/ per month.

To substantiate the income the Petitioner has not produced any relevant document to prove that she was getting income from doing Agriculture and milk vending such as the bank statement, agriculture produce sale bills or receipts etc., to ascertain her income and not examined any witness in this regard.
Therefore, the version of the Petitioner that she was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/ per month from agricultural work and milk vending, are not acceptable.
Therefore, the notional income needs to be considered.

At the time of accident the Petitioner was aged about 60 years as could be make out from Ex.P.9/Aadhar card of Smt.Rathnamma @ vs Sri.Harshit S on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166515967/
5 the petitioner.
The accident took place in the year 2020.

In absence of specific evidence for income,
therefore by taking judicial notice of the notified notional income chart approved by the KSLSA the monthly notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.14,500/ per month.

As such, Petitioner is entitled for the following compensation:
 i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:
After the accident, the Petitioner was taken to Adichunchanagiri Hospital, Mandya District, wherein admitted as an inpatient on 11.01.2020 to 05.02.2020 for 26 days as per Ex.P.7.

Therefore,
considering the nature of injuries and duration of treatment she has underwent, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.50,000/ under this head.
ii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained grievous injury in the accident and was taken treatment in the above mentioned hospital.
Therefore, considering the nature of injuries and the duration of treatment it can be said that the Petitioner has required at least two months time for recovering from the injuries sustained by her.
Hence, she is entitled for a sum of Rs.29,000/ under this head.
iii) MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner claimed that she incurred Rs.2,75,000/ towards medical expenses and produced prescriptions and 116 medical bills for Rs.62,087/ at Ex.P.8.
In the cross examination of PW.1 it is elicited that she not produced any prescriptions in support of Ex.P.8 medical bills.
But except this nothing worth is elicited to disbelieve the said medical bills.

Therefore,
the petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.62,087/ under this head.
iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:
In so far as age of the Petitioner is concerned, the Aadhar card and DL are is produced as per Exs.P.9 and P.10.
As per these document her age was 60 years as on the date of accident.
Therefore, as on the date of the accident the Petitioner's age is considered as 60 years.
As per the dictum laid down in Sarala Verma's case the appropriate multiplier applicable to her age is 9.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled a sum of Rs.2,19,240/ (Rs.14,500/ x 12 x 9 x 14%= Rs.2,19,240/) under this head.
(v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The Petitioner was aged about 60 years at the time of accident.

She has sustained grievous injuries and as per consideration of this Tribunal,
she is suffering from 14% permanent disability.
The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout her life.
Because of this she will have to lose some amenities and comforts.

Therefore,
considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered a sum of Rs.17,000/ is awarded under this head.

Smt.Rathnamma @ vs Sri.Harshit S on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166515967/
6 vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT CHARGES:

After the accident, the Petitioner took treatment in Adichunchanagiri Hospital,
Mandya District, wherein admitted as an inpatient for 26 days and underwent surgery.
Therefore, as during this period she must have spent considerable amount on her conveyance, attendant charges, food and nourishment etc..
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.17,000/ under this head.
vii) FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The PW.3 has deposed that, the petitioner needs another surgery for the implant removal and reconstruct the left elbow for which cost is estimated around Rs.1,20,000/.
The PW.3 has not given any estimation and deposed in details as to the future surgery.

Therefore, looking to the earlier treatment cost and nature of injuries and cross examination of PW.3, it appears it would be justifiable if an amount of Rs.20,000/ is awarded to the Petitioner under this head.
Therefore the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/ under this head.

18. The Petitioner is entitled compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.50,000/
2.

Medical expenses Rs.62,087/
3. Loss of income during laid up Rs.29,000/ period 4.

Loss of future income Rs.2,19,240/
5. Loss of future amenities and Rs.17,000/ happiness
6. Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.17,000/ nourishment charges 7.
Future medical expenses Rs.20,000/ TOTAL Rs.4,14,327/
If it is rounded off it comes to Rs.4,14,400/ and therefore, the total compensation comes to Rs.4,14,400/ and same is awarded to the petitioner under the above heads.
19. The Respondent No.2 has not proved its defence as discussed above.

Therefore,
the Respondent Nos.1 and 2 are being the owner and the Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
However, as the Petitioner has proved the existence of insurance policy, the Respondent No.2 - insurer has got primary liability to compensate the Petitioner.

The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.20,00,000/ but she is entitled only for a sum of Rs.4,14,400/ with interest @ 6% per Smt.Rathnamma @ vs Sri.Harshit S on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166515967/
7 annum from the date of petition till realization.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed in part.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is held partly in the affirmative.
20. Issue No.3:
For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following: ORDER
The petition is hereby allowed in part with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,14,400/ (Rupees Four Lakhs Fourteen Thousand and Four Hundred only) from the Respondents along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
The respondents 1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, the Respondent No.2 insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest within sixty days from the date of this Judgment.

On deposit of compensation and interest, as the petitioner is senior citizen and hence entire amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per rules.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw decree accordingly.
(Typed to my dictation directly on the computer by the Stenographer, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court on this the 19th day of January 2023).
(Miss B.T.ANNAPOORNESHWARI) C/c XXII Addl.
SCJ & ACMM Bengaluru.
